answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates from anchored identities through normalized, bounded-length random walks, with per-identity voting weight capped. A sybil cluster may wander internally, but a sparse external cut gives it low conductance and limits the probability mass reaching it from the trusted core. Its aggregate weight is therefore bounded by flow across the cut, not by fabricated node count. Like basalt resisting a pulse, this bottleneck limits amplification through transitive attestations.
